text:
Nora: I opened a small PR (adds an 'egress & TLS troubleshooting' appendix to private-deploy.md). Covers HSM egress testing, NAT asymmetry notes, HAProxy log examples, and two short SDK snippets (Node + Python). Need a quick docs review and a link-check sanity pass.
Sam: Sending the snippets here for quick eyeballs. Also call out vendor port (usually 16963/tcp for many appliance HSMs) and test steps.
Nora: Snippets: 
Nora: ```bash
# Check egress to HSM appliance from jump host
# replace <HSM_IP> and port per vendor
nc -vz 10.2.1.10 16963 || echo "egress blocked"

# node-level curl health check to HAProxy behind NAT
curl -sS -H 'Host: service.svc.internal' http://10.0.8.7:8080/health || tail -n 50 /var/log/haproxy.log

# Quick nftables SNAT check
sudo nft list table nat | sed -n '1,120p' | grep -Ei 'snat|masq' -A2
```
Ravi: For Kubernetes folks without a jumpbox add this invoker: `kubectl run --rm -i --tty busybox --image=busybox -- sh -c 'wget -qO- http://10.0.8.7:8080/health'` — simpler than complex jsonpath extraction.
Maya: Good. Please include an explicit note about asymmetric SNAT behavior: AWS NAT Gateway preserves source ports differently than GCE, which can affect client IP seen by on-prem HSM appliances. One-liner will save headaches.
Nora: Added a short paragraph about that and a tiny troubleshooting table (symptom -> quick check -> expected).
Sam: Can you paste the HAProxy log grep example? I want to keep it tiny for copy-paste.
Nora: ```
# HAProxy syslog example - grep for backend errors/latency
# example line format
Apr 30 10:02:11 haproxy[2544]: 10.0.8.7:38722 [30/Apr/2026:10:02:11.123] http-in~ backend/api/1 502/0/-1/25/30 0/0 "GET /health HTTP/1.1"
# grep command
grep "backend/api" /var/log/haproxy.log | tail -n 100
```
Ravi: Nice. Also include a one-liner systemd restart for haproxy in case folks need to rotate certs: `sudo systemctl restart haproxy && sudo journalctl -u haproxy -n 80 --no-pager`.
Nora: Added that. Also added SDK snippets: Node (dev TLS-fallback) and Python (requests-based egress probe).
Nora: ```js
// dev-only Node SDK TLS-fallback example (DO NOT USE IN PROD)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ baseUrl: 'https://localhost:8443', tls: { rejectUnauthorized: false } });
(async () => {
  try {
    const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'ping' });
    console.log(res.text.slice(0, 80));
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('proxy test failed', err.message);
  }
})();
```
Nora: ```py
# simple Python egress probe to HSM IP (requests)
import requests
try:
    r = requests.get('https://10.2.1.10:16963/', timeout=5, verify=False)
    print('reachable', r.status_code)
except Exception as e:
    print('egress failed', e)
```
Maya: Please ensure both snippets are explicitly labeled "dev-only" and we have the security caveat. Also mention TLS fingerprint differences for some HSM appliances.
Nora: Done. One more meta: CI link-check flagged a broken link in the PR to /docs/private/network/ports.md. We should point to /docs/networking/ports-reference.md instead.

Sam: Easy fix, update the reference and add a short commit message: "fix(link): point to networking/ports-reference.md". Call out in PR description that it's a link-fix commit.
Ravi: Quick nit — make the HAProxy example show a 5xx grep and a latency grep separately. Otherwise LGTM.
Nora: Split the grep lines per Ravi's suggestion and pushed a tiny commit. Also added a quick table row for "HSM TLS handshake fails" -> check clock skew, cert chain, and tcpdump on 16963.
Maya: I'll run link-check locally and do a light proofread. If green I'll approve.
